_purpose: The live GraphQL contract the belt-gateway PROMISES its consumers. Producer-side guard: CI introspects the live schema daily and fails the moment a consumer-depended field drifts or disappears. This catches the class of break where a consumer was built against an ASSUMED schema and only finds out in production — e.g. the Action_bool_exp input-type rename that froze purupuru's sync for 19 days in 2026-06, invisible because every consumer test mocks the wire.
_typeMapping: Hasura serves Envio BigInt as `numeric`, Int as `Int`, ID/String as `String`. Verified against the live endpoint 2026-07-31.
_history: Until 2026-07-31 this file guarded the `Transfer` entity for loa-freeside/packages/adapters/sonar (the Shadow-Mode audit). Both are gone — that adapter no longer exists in loa-freeside, and `Transfer` was one of the 91 orphan entities dropped from schema.graphql. The guard now covers the contract that actually has a consumer: score-api.

Action.consumer: score-api src/bronze/belt-gateway-source.ts PULL_QUERY — the bronze event pull that feeds all community scoring
invariants: The tx hash field here is `txHash`. On MintActivity it is `transactionHash`. The two entities disagree and both are load-bearing — do not 'fix' one without migrating its consumer in lockstep.
logIndex is NOT a column — it is encoded in id as `<txHash>_<logIndex>[_<suffix>]` and score-api derives it (parseLogIndex).
(timestamp, id) is the pull keyset. Changing either field's type or nullability breaks pagination, not just a projection.
blockNumber and transactionIndex are nullable: rows written before 2026-07-31 lack them. They give exact intra-block ordering, which (timestamp, id) alone cannot.

MintActivity.consumer: score-api src/silver/sale-attribution.ts — marketplace sale attribution (sale price facts, viaMarketplace stamping)
invariants: amountPaid is nullable by design: an unpriced sale is still a real disposal, and dropping it made 'sold' and 'could not price it' indistinguishable downstream.
amountPaid is the ROW TOTAL, not per unit — unit price is amountPaid / quantity.
paymentToken carries the settlement currency; the zero address means the chain's native coin. Without it, 1000 USDC and 1000 wei are indistinguishable.
